rows.label: Korrudo Blueprint
rows.note: 5% Tusk Thumper Bull, 10% Tusk Thumper Doma; Narmer versions drop it at the same rates

conditions: Thumpers spawn only in daytime, so the hunt is gated by the 150-minute Plains cycle.

Accept a Tier 5 (level 40-60) bounty only to set enemy levels, then ignore the objective. If the blueprint drops while the bounty runs, walk into the bounty area to activate it and leave to fail it before returning to Cetus, or the held reward is lost.
Kill it by shooting off the four knee plates, then the four glowing leg weak spots. Body hits do nothing.
bonuses: Nightwave kill-a-Thumper days are easier in a squad.
Narmer bounties, available after The New War, spawn Thumpers fast and often.

disclosures.title: finding them
disclosures.body: Fly low around the Plains and listen for the rumble; a Thumper erupts when you get close. Mount Nang camp and the seaside ruins are the most consistent spots, and Domas dominate the north half and further from the bounty entrance. Return to Cetus and re-enter to reset spawns. Spawn rates swing wildly: three in five minutes, or none in fifteen.

disclosures.title: killing them fast
disclosures.body: Slow or freeze it: Nova (Molecular Prime), Sevagoth (Gloom), Jade (Ophanim Eyes), Khora (Ensnare), Rhino Stomp, or Zenurik's Void Blast. Strip armor with Jade, Mag (Polarize), Caliban, Grendel, Nekros (Terrify) or a Shattering Impact weapon like Sarpa or Stropha. A Voidrig with Arquebex is the repeated melt-it answer; Jade plus Arquebex killed one in under half a minute on Steel Path. Boss-attenuation weapons like Felarx, Laetum Incarnon, Phenmor and Mausolon also work; rapid-fire hitscan beats AoE on the leg spots.

disclosures.title: pace
disclosures.body: Reports run from the first Thumper to 30+ and a year off and on. Update 42 doubled the rates from 2.5% and 5%, so older complaints overstate the grind. Farm a little each day rather than in marathons.
